⚡️🇮🇱🇵🇸 — Israel’s Shin Bet has allegedly threatened targets in Gaza with a choice between being killed alone or having their entire families bombed, according to a report by the London-based Arabic-language outlet Asharq Al-Awsat, THE JERUSALEM POST. 
➡️ The outlet said it interviewed several Palestinians it described as faction activists, along with their families, who reported similar experiences. The most recent alleged case involved Muhammad Al-Bayouk, who was reportedly called by a Shin Bet officer on Wednesday and told that either the shelter where his family was staying would be bombed or he would be targeted alone. He allegedly went to the roof of the shelter in Khan Younis and was killed by a small projectile launched from an Israeli drone.
➡️ A source told the outlet that the alleged targets were activists connected to military operations, while senior field commanders were targeted in larger strikes involving missiles and suicide drones, reportedly even when civilians were at risk.
➡️ The IDF and Shin Bet were not approached for comment, and the specific incidents described in the report could not be independently confirmed. The Jerusalem Post said it understood that similar operations had been conducted in the past.
➡️ Separately, the IDF announced that strikes on October 25 killed three Palestinian Islamic Jihad and Hamas operatives across Gaza. It also said four Islamic Jihad operatives had recently been killed in targeted strikes in Khan Younis.

events.text:
🇮🇷🚚 Iran Keeps Military Supplies Coming Despite US Sanctions
Iran has imported at least $2B in equipment, explosives and heavy trucks since January 2025 through more than 5,000 defense-linked agencies, according to Reuters investigation. Supplies kept arriving during the war, complicating US efforts to starve Iranian missile and drone factories of materials.
The buyers operate under numbered names beginning with MOD, short for Ministry of Defense. Most date to 2013, meaning Iran had years to build these channels before the fighting began. Despite decades of sanctions against Iran’s military, Reuters found no evidence that the numbered agencies it examined were themselves on Western sanctions lists.
Oil sales help pay the bills, with intermediaries and foreign shell companies using revenue held abroad to buy goods and send them home. For 97% of the shipments, the records showed settlement without a currency transfer. Keeping the money overseas reduces the need for cross-border payments that can trigger sanctions checks.
One buyer, MOD 346428, brought in rocket propellants, explosives, weapons components and heavy trucks between January 2025 and June 2026. These are the less photogenic essentials behind a missile launch: fuel, parts and vehicles that could carry launch equipment.
Deliveries came by land, sea and air, with much of the cargo listed as originating in China, Russia and Germany. A naval blockade cannot close every road or air route, and a product’s country of origin does not prove its manufacturer knowingly supplied Iran’s military.
Reuters examined bank records, corporate filings and import data, cross-checking part of some 19,000 import records. Many goods also have civilian uses, so a shipment of components cannot be counted as a batch of finished missiles. The records do not establish whether Iran is replacing weapons as fast as it fires them.
The US Treasury told Reuters it was “10 steps ahead,” a confident assessment for an enforcement effort still watching supplies get through. The findings show how Iran has kept buying despite restrictions, even if they do not show that sanctions leave it unscathed.
Iran’s continued access to military supplies exposes the gap between US pressure and US control. Sanctions and a naval blockade have failed to seal off its procurement network, leaving Iran able to bring in materials for weapons production even during the war.

🇺🇸 Israelis offer a choice of death to Palestinians in Gaza – report
Israeli forces have adopted a practice of killing Palestinians that involves calling the victims beforehand and offering them a choice of getting bombed together with their relatives or moving to a spot where they could be killed alone, according to media reports.
In one such instance earlier this week, a young Palestinian man, Mohammed al-Bayouk ended up going to the roof of the shelter where he was living with his family to be killed by a missile in order to ensure that his relatives don’t get killed as well.
One of al-Bayouk’s aunts was injured during the attack as she attempted to stop him from going to the site of his eventual killing.
At least five such killings were ostensibly perpetrated by the Israelis in Gaza over the past three months.
A similar incident was reported back in February in Lebanon, where a 62-year-old man named Ahmad Tarmous was killed by an Israeli drone strike minutes after receiving a similar threat from the Israelis.
